### Observed differences

- The order at the end of the traces reversed. In the earlier window, all 200 traces ended with the sequence A08 → A06 → A07 → A01: A01 was the final activity and showed no observed successor, A07 was followed by A01 in all 200 of its observed outgoing transitions, and A06 preceded A01 in 100% of traces. In the later window, every trace runs A08 → A01 → A06 → A07: A01's only observed successor is now A06 (all 200 observed transitions), A08's observed successor changed from A06 to A01, and A01 precedes both A06 and A07 in 100% of traces. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002]
- Event positions shifted accordingly: A01's mean position fell from 1.0 (always last) to about 0.71, while A06 and A07 each moved one position later (about 0.71 → 0.86 and 0.86 → 1.0, so A07 is now the final activity); the spread is zero in both windows, so the order is identical in every trace within each window. [POS001, POS002, POS003]
- Distances changed exactly as this single reordering predicts: A01 moved two steps closer to A03, A05 and A08 (A08→A01 from 3 to 1 steps, A03→A01 from 4 to 2, A05→A01 from 5 to 3), while A06 and A07 moved one step further from the same upstream activities (for example A08→A06 from 1 to 2, A04→A06 from 4 to 5, A03→A07 from 3 to 4). [LAG001, LAG005, LAG008, LAG002, LAG004, LAG003]
- Participation did not change: A01, A06 and A07 occur in all traces in both windows (200 of 200), and within each window the order shares are exactly 100% versus 0%, so this is a uniform reversal of execution order, not a shift in how often activities run or in the mix of variants. [POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 and the consecutive pair A06 → A07 exchanged their order at the end of the process: in the earlier window A01 executed after A07 as the final activity (tail A08 → A06 → A07 → A01), whereas in the later window A01 executes directly after A08 and before A06 and A07 (tail A08 → A01 → A06 → A07), with A06 and A07 keeping their mutual order but each moving one position later. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002, POS001, POS002, POS003]

The order change is shown directly by the relational items (A06 and A07 before A01 in 100% of earlier traces versus A01 before both in 100% of later traces, each backed by 200 traces per window) and by the successor changes at A01, A07 and A08; all ten lag items quantitatively match one and the same two-position shift of A01, and every item shows the same top reference strength (differences larger than in about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits). [REL001, REL002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, POS001, POS002, POS003]

Limitations: the indicators describe the same traces, so the agreeing items are not independent confirmations; positions and lags are measured in event positions, so no statement about clock-time timing is possible; and the packet provides no screening expectation against which to compare the item count. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that this reversal is the visible part of a broader restructuring that also involves the activities preceding A04, which the evidence does not cover. [POS001, POS002, POS003, LAG001, LAG004, LAG005, REL001]

Other differences: none — all 18 items describe the same reordering of A01 relative to A06 and A07 rather than separate changes. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]
